- `_fields` is not advertised (use `fields`).
- A call runs through the member's own tools, so scopes, views, repairs and the journal are the member's.
`hybrid` adds the guide's recipes (below). A caller whose every API is grouped sees six tools: the three group tools, `api_search`, `api_describe`, `api_result_query` (plus the recipes in hybrid).
On the gateway, the profile editor's serving mode select sets the mode per product row (`model`, `compact`, `minimal`, `group`, `hybrid`, `per_operation`; migration 0030 stores all six). A product row whose id is a group id (`cw_psa_*`) is refused with a 400 (`cw_psa_* is a group: add its member products`); add the member products instead. An `apis.yaml` import expands a group entry into one product row per stored member and writes each scope's mode for a catalog, else the entry's. The console import wizard's mode select is ignored by the import: the serving mode is chosen on the profile. The profile preview (`GET /api/v1/profiles/{id}/preview` and `/me/access`) is the same tool list `tools/list` serves (`connector_core::tools::visible`), so a product saved `compact`, `group` or `hybrid` previews those tools and their token estimate. The catalog breakdown tab still generates the model view of that one catalog (it has no profile and no group).

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Guides
sections.text:
A guide (`pulsatrix-guide/1`, ` /guides/ .guide.json`) is the vendor knowledge of one catalog or one registry group: where things are (`routing`), filter and naming conventions, time rules, per-resource views, labels, search fields, aliases and hints, write rules, policy lines, `hide` globs, `serve.fold_model` and recipes. Format and rules: section 3 of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-23-small-model-surface-plan.md`, and `docs/catalog-format.md`.
What a caller sees of it, rendered in their own naming and narrowed to what their scopes reach (a line naming a hidden resource is dropped):
| Where | What |
 
| Query tool description, under `Guide:` | the scope line (`Scope: served here: ...`), routing, conventions, the time sentence |
| Write tool description, under `Guide:` | write lines, policy lines |
| `api_describe` card, `guide` block | the resource's hints, view, label and search fields |
| Error hints | label and search fields first among the closest names; the parent hint |
| `instructions` | the scope line, the time sentence and the policy lines only |
| Behind the scenes | the name ranker (aliases, labels, metadata paths), `api_search` (resource words such as `billet`, `technicien`), `identity` (search fields), the default view, the group enums |
An operator installs a guide, except a starter guide marked `install: auto` (SentinelOne's), which the connector seeds once, at boot or reload, when its catalog is imported; removing it is permanent. `pulsatrix-connector guide import ` (then `api_reload` or restart), `guide list`, `guide show [--naming compact|model|minimal|per_operation|group|hybrid]`, `guide remove `; or the Guide panel of a product page in the console (upload, or the starter guide of `catalog/guides/`), backed by `/api/v1/guides`. `check` prints one budget line per guide.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Jev bridge: `<api>__ask` (opt-in)
sections.text:
Design and data posture: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-28-jev-bridge-design.md`. A catalog product the gateway answers through Jev (`PUT /api/v1/products/{id}/bridge`, or `apis[].bridge` in `apis.yaml`) serves ` __ask`, only to a caller whose profile product sets `ask: true` (false by default; a scope's `ask` list in `apis.yaml`). Anyone else is neither listed it nor able to call it, and nothing is sent to Jev for them.
 `{ "request": "show me widget 42", "arguments": { }, "operation": "getWidget", "confirm": true, "_dry_run": false }` 
`request` is plain language; `arguments` the values already known (body fields under `body`); `operation` runs one operation of an earlier answer without routing. Jev picks one exposed operation the caller is granted and fills its missing required parameters from the request; when confident, exactly one call is made and the answer carries `called: true`, `chosen`, `arguments`, `jev` (the confidences) and the operation's result. Otherwise `called: false`, `sent: false`, `reasons`, `candidates` and `ambiguous`, and nothing reached the API.
Sent off the machine, to `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` with the product's Jev key: the request text (at most 4000 bytes), the caller's `arguments`, per candidate operation its id, method, path, summary and required argument names, and the candidate values extracted from the request. Never the API credential, its base URL or a vendor response.
Writes (`!op.is_read()`) are always held for a confirmation first, whatever the confirm set says and even when the caller names the `operation`: the first call answers a preview; repeat the same `operation` and `arguments` with `confirm: true` after the user said yes. On an operation whose vendor declares its own `confirm`, that one stays in `arguments` and goes to the vendor as given.
Journal: the ask row names the operation chosen in `op`; under it (`parent_request_id`) one row of kind `bridge` records the product, the operation, the Jev requests (`vendor_calls`), the bytes sent to Jev (`bytes_out`) and received (`bytes_in`), never the text.
The Jev key is a credential of `purpose: bridge`: not listed by `GET /api/v1/credentials`, never bound, never a default, removed with the bridge.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: MCP Apps: the ConnectWise views (`io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`)
sections.text:
Perspicax serves four interactive views of ConnectWise PSA to a host that implements MCP Apps (SEP-1865, specification 2026-01-26, the stable version of `modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`; Claude Desktop today, Sagax once its host is ready). Code: `crates/connector/src/mcp/apps.rs`; the views: `crates/connector/assets/mcp-apps/` (`shell.html`, `app.css`, `app.js`, composed into one document per view by `apps::html`).
Negotiation. Everything below is served only to a client that declares the extension with the HTML type: `capabilities.extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/ui"].mimeTypes` containing `text/html;profile=mcp-app`, in `initialize` (2025-11-25) or in the request `_meta` (2026-07-28). The server then names the same extension in its own capabilities (`initialize`, `server/discover`). A client that does not declare it is served exactly what it was before: no `_meta` on any tool or result, no `ui://` resource in `resources/list`.
| View | URI | Recipe that carries it (`_meta.ui.resourceUri`) |
 
| One ticket with its notes | `ui://perspicax/cw/ticket` | `cw_psa__get_ticket` |
| A list of tickets | `ui://perspicax/cw/tickets` | `cw_psa__find_tickets` |
| Time entries | `ui://perspicax/cw/time-entries` | `cw_psa__find_time_entries` |
| A technician's schedule by day | `ui://perspicax/cw/schedule` | `cw_psa__find_schedule_entries` |
The recipes exist in hybrid mode only (Recipes above), so a profile in another mode has no view. A tool carries `_meta.ui = { resourceUri, visibility: ["model", "app"] }` and the deprecated flat `_meta["ui/resourceUri"]` the SDK still writes; a view is listed and read only for a caller whose listing holds its recipe. `resources/read` of a view answers `text/html;profile=mcp-app` whatever the client declared (a host may prefetch).
A template, no data. Each view is one HTML document, CSS and script inline, the same bytes for every caller. Its `_meta.ui.csp` declares no origin (`connectDomains`, `resourceDomains`, `frameDomains`, `baseUriDomains` empty, no `permissions`), so the host applies the restrictive default of the specification, and the document carries its own ` ` policy (`default-src 'none'`, `connect-src 'none'`, inline script and style only, images from `data:` only). The view draws vendor text with `textContent`, never as markup. The data is the tool result the host hands the view (`ui/notifications/tool-result`); a result behind a handle is read through the caller's own `api_result_query`.
The view's `_meta` on a result. A recipe that carries a view answers, for a client with the extension, the same `content` and `structuredContent` as before plus `_meta["ca.pulsatrix.perspicax/ui"]`:
 
`timeZone` is the caller's (their profile's, else the deployment's; `null` when neither sets one, the vendor's UTC then). `locale` is the person's language in the directory (else the view reads the host's `locale`, then the browser's): French or English.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface
sections.text:
Date: 2026-09-28 (MCP Apps section 2026-10-14)
Role: what a client actually calls on `/mcp` today. Verified against `crates/connector-core/src/tools/`, `crates/connector-core/src/guide/`, `crates/connector-core/src/call/confirm.rs`, `crates/connector-core/src/call/time.rs` and `crates/connector/src/mcp/`. Design history lives in `AGENTS.md` (v2 retirement increments B, C, D), the spec and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-23-small-model-surface-plan.md` (DEC-1 to DEC-14); this page is the operator and developer cheat sheet.
Perspicax is the API to MCP layer. Any MCP client connects to `/mcp` directly and is served the same surface; Bifrost is one client recipe among others (`docs/bifrost-connect.md`). Some clients (Bifrost, Open WebUI) drop the MCP `instructions`, so everything a tool needs to be used well rides in its own description, in `api_describe` cards and in error hints; the instructions only repeat the scope, time and policy lines.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Meta-tools
sections.text:
| Tool | What it does | Cap |
 
| `api_list` | APIs the caller can reach (id, catalog `title`, and `display_name` when an admin named the product) | |
| `api_search` | Ranked operations in that set; each hit names the caller's own tool and the `resource` or `action` to pass it; zero hits answer a hint naming the served APIs | |
| `api_describe` | An operation id, a query resource name, ` _write`, a compact action name or a group spelling; `api` optional (an ambiguous name is refused listing the APIs). The query-hint spelling `api_describe ` and the tool spelling ` __ ` are both accepted as `op_id` when the head is an API the caller is served (`split_api_prefix`). A resource answers a card: verbs, the caller's tool, fields, writable and required fields, references and whether they take a name, `expandable`, sub-resources, parent, view, date ranges, the operation note, the guide block. An unknown name answers `details.closest` | |
| `api_reload` | Re-read catalogs and guides and notify `tools/list_changed` when the tool hash changed (every tool is hashed, its name included, so a renamed catalog with the same tool count notifies too: `listen_receives_tools_list_changed_after_a_catalog_rename`). Bundled mode, and an active gateway admin, only. Anyone else is refused as an unknown tool and does not see it in `tools/list` | |
| `api_result_query` | JMESPath over a handle (200 ms, 64 MiB) | |
| `api_lookup` | Named lookup tables; answer always carries `as_of` | |
| `api_plan` | Read tools for real, writes as `_dry_run`; refuses meta-tools | 20 steps |
| `api_upload` | Reserve a slot for one file (`filename`, `bytes`, `sha256`, optional `content_type`); the answer gives the `upload` id, a `PUT /uploads` with `Authorization: Upload ` and a ready `curl` line. Listed and run only for a caller that reaches an exposed multipart operation (issue #147) | 16 MiB per file, 64 MiB for all slots, 8 slots per caller, 10 minutes |
| `identity` | `contains` over the identity fields and a guide's search fields of top-level resources (a family under a path placeholder is skipped), plus lookup names; its description names what it searches; listed only when there is something to search | 20 vendor calls |
`api_plan` stops at the first failure. A tool the caller cannot see is unknown. `PUT /uploads` needs no bearer: the slot token is its only authority, compared hashed, one PUT per slot, the length and the SHA-256 checked against what `api_upload` declared (a mismatch deletes the slot), any `Origin` refused; the bytes stay in memory, bound to the caller's `sub`, and are gone on restart. Every meta-tool call is journaled (kind `meta`); the `api_upload` row keeps the slot id and never the token; the vendor calls of `identity` and `api_lookup` sit under that row, and each `api_plan` step names the plan as its parent request.
### Claim tools

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Pitfalls
sections.text:
- Empty env vars and whitespace-only files are missing secrets, not empty credentials. `check` prints `unavailable`.
- Asio (`cw_rmm`) token requests need `client_auth: json_body`. Form-encoded answers `400 failed to decode request invalid JSON`.
- ScreenConnect query takes `args`, not `filter`.
- A profile that grants two of 380 PSA operations still lists only those two resources on the query tool (and on a group query tool). Calling anything else reads as unknown.
- `?profile= ` on `/mcp` narrows the token to that one `profile: ` scope. A slug the caller does not hold answers the same 401 as a bad bearer.
- One Manage credential bound to `cw_psa_*` covers every `cw_psa_*` module. A second key per sibling is not required.
- `fields` is what each item keeps. Ask for the fields you will read; `fields: "*"` is the raw object, which is large.
- `expand` reaches the resources of the same catalog only, except through a group query tool, which also follows a reference into a sibling member. `board`, `status`, `type` and the other references served by `cw_psa_service` expand.
- A write tool says which reference types take a name: only those the product declares a lookup for. With no lookups declared, every reference takes `{ "id": .. }` and `api_lookup` has nothing to list. On a gateway deployment an admin edits a product's lookups in the console (product sheet, tab Correspondances) or with `PUT /api/v1/products/{id}/lookups` (`{ "lookups": { " ": { "op", "key", "parent"?, "search"? } } }`, the whole list replaced, an empty object removes it): checked against the product's catalog with the registry import's rule (`op` a GET of that catalog, `search` one of its query parameters, `key` not empty), the type a catalog schema name, at most 100 lookups, one `product.lookups` audit row, refusals audited (issue #140).
- A sub-resource (`notes` under `tickets`, `associations` under a board item) is queried with `parent`; without it the refusal names the resource and its parent. A top-level resource refuses `parent`.
- Manage files live on `documents`, not `attachments`. `attachments` has a get and no list: query `documents` with `filter.recordType` and `filter.recordId` (vendor selectors, above). Those keys are not fields of DocumentInfo; putting them in `filter` as equality is the supported call.
- A refused write carries the corrected call in `details.suggested`: it was not sent. Re-send it, do not assume it ran.
- With a confirmation configured, the first delete answers a preview and `sent: false`. The user's request is not the confirmation; ask, then repeat with `confirm: true`.
- Upgrading past the SentinelOne literal: import `catalog/guides/sentinelone.guide.json`, or a model caller gets SentinelOne's whole model view (`check` warns above 150 tools).
- Do not invent vendor field names. Use `api_describe`, the notes file and the guide.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Provenance
sections.text:
`as_of` (RFC 3339 seconds) is present only when the answer did not come from the vendor at this instant: a replayed fixture, or a hit on the reference cache (`call/ref_cache.rs`). `api_lookup` always carries `as_of`. A write that resolved a name carries `resolved: [{ field, name, id, as_of }]`.
The reference cache answers some Manage list tables (`cw_conditions` vocabulary, or a notes `cache_ttl_seconds`) for `eq` / `in` / `null` / `not_null` only. A write evicts every cached table whose family prefixes the written path.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Query: `<api>__query`
sections.text:
| Argument | Role |
 
| `resource` | Model resource name (the enum is narrowed to what the caller can reach) |
| `id` | Get one object |
| `parent` | Required on a sub-resource (a resource whose family sits under another object, `/tickets/{parentId}/notes`): the id of that object, or an array of ids outermost first when the family has two placeholders. Refused by name before any call when missing, one too many, not of the placeholder's type, or given on a top-level resource |
| `filter` | Dialect grammar (below). A `positional_rpc` catalog takes `args` instead |
| `fields` | What each item keeps: an array, or one comma-separated string of dotted paths. The items are projected on exactly these paths (plus `id`, plus the `include` and `expand` names) whether or not the vendor received them; also sent to the vendor when the dialect hands `fields` over and the operation declares the parameter. `"*"` or `["*"]`: the raw vendor object, no vendor `fields` sent. Absent, with no `_fields`: the default view, whose own fields go to the vendor in its place |
| `_fields` | The same projection, applied by the connector only; an array, or one comma-separated string of dotted paths; `"*"` or `["*"]` returns the raw item. Accepted in every mode, not advertised in group and hybrid. With both, `_fields` decides the local projection and `fields` the vendor one |
| `_format` | `objects` (default) or `table` |
| `include`, `expand` | Fan-out, capped at 20 extra calls (`FANOUT_MAX`), four in flight. What it fetches survives the default view, reduced through the target resource's own view. `include` takes the sub-resource's name (`notes`) or its resource-enum spelling (`tickets_notes`); `expand` takes only the reference fields that resolve (`api_describe` lists them as `expandable`); another reference is already `{ id, name }` in each item, so it is left out and reported in `_repaired` (`expand_not_needed`); an unknown name is refused with the closest ones before any call |
| `order`, `limit`, `cursor` | Dialect paging. `order` takes several comma-separated fields, each `field` or `field asc|desc`. `limit` is 1 to 1000 (`QUERY_LIMIT_MAX`); `_limit` is the same argument |
An unknown argument is refused with the three closest declared names and the argument list; an unknown resource with the closest resource names and, when the api came from a registry group (`cw_psa_*`), the sibling query tool that serves that name, if the caller's scopes reach it there.
A query without `limit` on a resource that has a count verb answers with the count and a hint once the match set is above 200 (`COUNT_BUDGET`). `total` is that count when one ran, else the number of items when the list was read whole (`next` null and not cut by `limit`), else null; a get by id carries none.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Recipes (hybrid)
sections.text:
A recipe is a task tool a guide declares under `tasks`, served in hybrid only as ` __ ` (or ` __ ` for an API without a group). It is one read or one write of one resource with flat scalar parameters: no template, no guard, no loop (not a spec D18 macro).
 `{ "owner": "Julie", "state": "open", "entered_after": "2026-09-01", "limit": 25 }` 
- A name given for a reference (`owner`, `company`, `board`, `member`) is resolved on its target with one `contains` query per match field, plus, for a text of two words or more on a target matched by `firstName` and `lastName`, one query with the first word on the first name and the last word on the last name (`Julie Tremblay` is in no single field); a value made of digits is an id. Several candidates are refused with `details.candidates` (at most 10 `{ id, label }`).
- A list answers `{ items, next, total, applied, excluded_by_default? }`, a get `{ item, applied }`, a create or update the write result plus `applied`. `applied` names every filter that took effect, defaults included (`"state": "open (closedFlag false)"`). `excluded_by_default` counts what a default left out, when the profile grants the count.
- Every field a parameter filtered or ordered on is returned, beyond the recipe's own `fields`.
- `period` parameters (`today`, `yesterday`, `tomorrow`, `this_week`, `last_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `last_month`) follow the caller's time zone and `week_start`: their profile's when it sets one, else the deployment's (UTC and Monday without one).
- A recipe is listed only when the caller's scopes grant its target's verb and the list of every resolve target. Writes go through the confirmation like any write.
The cw_psa starter guide carries twelve: `find_tickets`, `get_ticket`, `update_ticket`, `find_schedule_entries`, `book_schedule_entry`, `find_time_entries`, `log_time`, `find_project_tickets`, `find_members`, `find_companies`, `find_agreements`, `find_opportunities`.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Time zone
sections.text:
Set `time_zone` (an IANA name, `America/Toronto`) and `week_start` (`monday` to `sunday`, default `monday`) in `config.toml`, or in the gateway settings (the Status page's time card), which win when they set a zone.
A profile can set its own (issue #139): `time_zone` and `week_start` on `PATCH /api/v1/profiles/{id}` (admins; the profile's General tab), validated like the settings, an empty string clearing either, a `week_start` without a zone refused. The gateway writes them on the profile's scope (`scopes. .time_zone` and `week_start` of the registry, validated the same way), and every caller holding that profile is served that zone instead of the deployment's: the conversions of what they write and query, the results they read, the recipe periods and parameters, the query tools' Times sentence and the instructions (`ScopeGate::time_for`). A profile `week_start` left empty takes the deployment's, else Monday. A caller whose profiles set two different zones, or none, is served the deployment's. The profile preview reads the profile's zone the same way.
- Always: a date-time with an offset is sent as the same instant in `Z` (`time_offset`).
- With a zone: a naive date-time (`2026-09-23T09:00:00`, also `2026-09-23T09:00` or `2026-09-23 09:00` with a space for the `T`) on a date-time field is read in the zone (`time_local`); a date-only value on a date-time field becomes its local day (`eq D` is the whole day, `lte D` the end of it; `time_local_day`); a write converts the same way (`converted`); results show date-times in the zone with their offset (`2026-09-23T09:00:00-04:00`), except `fields: "*"` and `_fields: "*"`; recipe periods and weeks follow the zone.
- A field is a date-time when its schema says `format: date-time`, or when it has no format, is not a boolean, number, object or array, and has a date name or is listed in the guide's `time.date_time_fields`. A `format: date` field is never converted.
- The query tools carry one sentence: `Times: the vendor stores UTC; this deployment's time zone is America/Toronto and weeks start on Monday. Pass local times without an offset and the connector converts them; results show local times with their offset.` Without a zone, a guide with `time.wire: utc` gives `Times: the vendor stores and expects UTC (ISO 8601 with Z).`
- Without a zone, naive values pass as they always did.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Tool name style
sections.text:
Every tool is named ` __ ` inside the connector, the head being an api id or a group name (`cw_psa_service__tickets_write`, `cw_psa__write`, `sentinelone__ask`). A client that prefixes its own ` __` and drops a tool name holding a second `__` (Grok, issue #85) sees none of them. `tool_name_separator = "-"` in `config.toml` (one value for the whole deployment; `"__"` is the default and changes nothing) makes `/mcp` advertise ` - ` instead:
- `tools/list` names every such tool with `-` (`cw_psa_service-tickets_write`) and rewrites the ` __` spellings in its title, its description and the `description` strings of its input schema; the meta-tools keep their names (`api_plan`).
- The instructions, every meta-tool answer (`api_search` hits, `api_describe` cards, `api_plan` steps) and every error (hints) spell the tools the same way. A ` __` is rewritten only when ` ` is a whole word that is a served api id, a group name or the head of a served tool, so a filter such as `createdAt__gt` is left alone. A generated tool's successful answer is the vendor's data and is never rewritten.
- `tools/call` accepts both spellings, and so do an `api_plan` step's `tool` and `api_describe`'s `op_id`. Everything behind the boundary uses the internal name: dispatch, the journal, the audit, the console and the profile preview still show `__`.
- `-` and not `.`: both are legal in an MCP tool name (2025-11-25: `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - .`), but the function names of the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, which many clients copy MCP tools into, allow `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -` only.
`api_plan` previews every write as a `_dry_run` by design (section Meta-tools): it never sends one, and `_dry_run: false` in a step does not change that. A write is sent by calling its own tool.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: What `tools/list` contains
sections.text:
Per served catalog, in this order:
1. One ` __query` tool.
2. Write tools: ` __ _write` in model mode, or one ` __write` in compact mode.
3. Action tools: one per leftover operation in model mode, or in compact mode one ` __action` for the write actions and one ` __read_action` (readOnlyHint true) for the read-only ones: a GET such as an OData function (3CX `Pbx.GetLogs(...)`) or a download.
In group and hybrid mode the members of one registry group (`cw_psa_*`) are served by three tools of the group instead, ` __query`, ` __write` and ` __action` (`cw_psa__query`), listed where the group id sorts among the API ids, followed in hybrid by the guide's recipes (`cw_psa__find_tickets`). Then the meta-tools.
| Mode | Per API (or per group) | Meta-tools listed |
 
| `model` (default) | query, one write tool per writable resource, one action tool per leftover operation | the seven below, plus `identity` when its sweep is not empty and `api_upload` when the caller reaches a multipart operation |
| `compact` | query, ` __write`, ` __action` | same |
| `minimal` | query only | same |
| `per_operation` | one tool per operation, with the vendor `body` | same |
| `group` | per group the three group tools; an API with no registry group gets its compact view | `api_search`, `api_describe`, `api_result_query` when every API the caller reaches is grouped, else as above |
| `hybrid` | `group` plus the guide's recipes (an API with no group: compact plus its recipes) | as `group` |
The seven: `api_list`, `api_search`, `api_describe`, `api_reload`, `api_result_query`, `api_lookup`, `api_plan`. `api_reload` is left out, and refused as an unknown tool, unless the caller may rebuild the runtime (a bundled server, or an active admin under gateway management). A meta-tool left out of a group caller's list still runs when called by name (DEC-2: nothing is removed from a profile, only unlisted). `review_write` is listed only while ` /write_approvals.yaml` is loaded (Write approvals below); without a policy the name is an unknown tool.
A token only sees APIs its scopes grant. A denied operation is indistinguishable from an unknown one (`params_invalid` / unknown tool wording).
`mode: per_operation` (an `apis.yaml` entry) keeps one tool per operation and never switches.
A bridged API (the Jev bridge, below) adds one ` __ask` after its own tools, in every mode, once per API also when it is served through a group, and only for a caller whose profile opts in.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Write approvals (bot accounts)
sections.text:
Distinct from Confirmation: that preview is confirmed by the same caller with `confirm: true`. A write-approval preview is decided by another account through `review_write`. When ` /write_approvals.yaml` lists the caller's subject, a matching write is held for `review_write` first. An approved write still runs through Confirmation (DEC-4) and the session rule of `bulk`. `_dry_run: true` is never held. There is no `alwaysAllow`. A write that matches no rule is refused (`params_invalid`, nothing sent). The file is optional: missing means the connector behaves as it did. A file that does not parse refuses boot (`write_approvals.yaml: ...`). Unknown keys, `alwaysAllow` included, are refused at parse.
Copy the documented dispatch example from `docs/write-approvals.yaml` (generic placeholder names):
 
`owner` is the account that may approve a rule whose `approver` is `owner`. The dispatch example names a generic cabinet-chief bot instead (`approver: { bot: chef-de-cabinet }`). `accounts. ` is the MCP token subject. Each rule names:
| Field | Meaning |
 
| `tool` | The write tool name, or `*` |
| `resource_prefix` | ConnectWise family (`schedule/entries`) or the resource name; `.` and leading `/` are equivalent |
| `operation` | `create`, `update` or `delete` |
| `path` | Vendor path prefix; `/` matches every path of that resource |
| `approver` | `owner`, or `{ bot: " " }` for another MCP caller |
Deletes are omitted in the dispatch example, so they are refused. A matching write sends nothing: it runs as a dry run, keeps a pending entry for 15 minutes (`call::write_approvals::WINDOW`, 64 per writer) and answers, not as an error:
 
The named approver calls `review_write` with `{ "id", "decision": "approve" | "refuse" }`. Approve runs the original write as the writer, with Confirmation and the bulk session rule still in force; refuse drops it. An unknown or expired id, a caller who is not the approver, and the writer of the pending call (no self-approval, even when the rule names them) are `params_invalid`. The journal records a pending write with outcome `pending`. Reload keeps the pending store, the way Confirmation keeps its previews. The gate applies to every write path: write tools (model, compact, group, recipe), action tools, compact and group actions, `per_operation` operations, and a Jev ask that would write. A read is not gated.

sections.title: Perspicax: MCP tool surface: Writes: `<api>__<resource>_write`
sections.text:
`set` is an open object. Writable names are checked at call time (`validate_set`), and a write is never rewritten by a guess: every problem is collected into one `params_invalid` (`set has N problems`) with `details.problems` (`{ field, problem, closest }`), `details.missing` (required fields a create lacks) and, when a mechanical fix exists, `details.suggested` = `{ tool, arguments }`, the whole call with every fix applied (a misspelled or aliased key replaced, `status: 13` or `statusId: 13` written `status: { "id": 13 }`, a wrapping quote pair removed). Nothing is sent; call again with the suggested arguments. A reference takes a name (resolved through lookups, only for the reference types the product declares a lookup for) or `{ "id": ... }`. `api_describe _write` lists the writable fields and whether the resource needs `parent`.
| Constraint | Value |
 
| `action` | `create`, `update`, `delete` |
| `ids` | At most 100 objects (`WRITE_IDS_MAX`), one audit line each |
| `parent` | Required on a sub-resource (`/tickets/{parentId}/notes`); the refusal names the resource and what it sits under |
| `_dry_run` | Builds the request and does not send it |
| `confirm` | Present only when the deployment holds this kind of write (see Confirmation) |
| `write_approvals.yaml` | A listed bot account may write only when a rule matches; a match waits for `review_write` (see Write approvals) |
| `fields` cap | `apis[].expose.fields` and a scope's `products. .fields` intersect; checked in `call/execute.rs` on the prepared body |
An operation with no request body takes no `set` (example: `cw_psa_time__reverse_write`). A non-empty `set` there is refused by name; `set: {}` is the same as omitting it.
A multipart file field (`system.documents` create, the SentinelOne uploads) takes `{ "upload": "upl_…" }` from `api_upload` (optional `filename` and `content_type` overrides), or a path under the config dir as a string or `{ path, filename, content_type }`. A dry run resolves the upload and echoes `source: "upload:upl_…"`, the size and the SHA-256 without spending it; the vendor's 2xx spends it, a refusal keeps it for a retry.
Under a deployment time zone, a naive local date-time in `set` is converted and listed in the result entry's `converted`.
SentinelOne `{ data, filter }` actions (a body of exactly `data` plus an object `filter` that declares `ids`) take `ids` (vendor `maxItems`, else 5000) or a query-tool `filter`, plus `data`. Both, neither, an empty `ids`, or a filter that compiles to `{}` are refused before any request.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): ask_person (A.2)
sections.text:
Nobody reads another person's tier; a client asks the person instead. The
question (at most 1 000 characters, gated) is recorded, one line goes to the
asker's work log (the topic, never the text), and the question is delivered
by the person's channel: their Sagax (a nudge through the member API) when a
server is linked, else email, or an https webhook an admin sets (person
sheet). The link ` /console/memory/ask/ ` opens the answer
form; a linked Sagax may answer for the person with
`POST /api/v1/memory/questions/{id}/sagax-answer` under its link token
(`{ "person": " ", "answer": "..." }`). The answer becomes a `humain`
entry of the asker's tier authored by the person who answered, who may
propose it to a team at once (`propose_to`); the asker can share it later
with `memory_promote`. A failed delivery leaves the question recorded
(`delivery: failed`).

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Audiences (A.2)
sections.text:
The scope of a `memory_write` comes, in order, from its `scope` argument
(Sagax sends the bot's audience this way), the default of the profile the
call is narrowed to (`?profile=`, or a token that holds one profile), the
person's default, else `me`. Defaults are set in the console (person sheet,
profile page) or with `PUT /api/v1/memory/admin/people/{id}` and
`PUT /api/v1/memory/admin/profiles/{id}/audience`. A default naming a team
the person left falls back to `me` (the answer says so); an explicit scope
they cannot write is refused.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Backup and restore
sections.text:
Each database backup (`gateway backup`, the nightly loop) takes the memory
write lock and writes, with the database copy's own stamp, into
` /backups/`:
- `memory- - .tar.gz`: `users/`, `work/`, `proposals/`, `archive/`;
- `memory- - .bundle`: `git bundle --all` of `org/` and `teams/`.
Both rotate with the database copies. Restore into a fresh config directory:

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Console (A.2)
sections.text:
Mémoire > Propositions (managers and admins: the queue with filters, risk
badges, bulk approval of safe items, a sheet to approve, edit, merge,
refuse or return), Mémoire > Tags (admins: namespaces, values, sources and
sync, the directory switch per team, the governance settings), the answer
form `/console/memory/ask/ `, the Mémoire card of a person's sheet
(audience, ask channel, export, erase) and the default audience on a
profile.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Console (A.5)
sections.text:
Lot A.5 completes the section (admins unless said otherwise):
- Propositions: a search over title, topic, tier and author, the risk
 score on each badge (`(3)`; risky from 2), a box that picks every safe
 item for a bulk approval.
- Étiquettes: a search over the namespaces; the review settings moved to
 Politiques.
- Personnes (`/memory/people`): every directory person with the size of
 their tier, their last write (from the audit), their default audience,
 their ask channel, what waits and their shared contributions; a row opens
 the person's Mémoire card (audience, channel, export, erasure). Never
 content.
- Politiques (`/memory/policies`, `GET` and `PUT
 /api/v1/memory/admin/policies`): the namespaces required on shared
 writes; auto-accept per tier (`members` or `never` for teams, `admins` or
 `never` for org; a `tiers` source is always reviewed); the review cap,
 expiry and injection budget; the stale threshold (180 days); a PII action
 per category (`allow`, `mask`, `quarantine`, `refuse`; read by the filter
 of lot A.3); the consolidation schedule (enabled, `HH:MM`, days; read by
 lot A.6). Every change is an `admin_audit` row per setting.
- Quarantaine (`/memory/quarantine`): the writes the gate refused, with the
 rule, the sha256 of the text, the author, the operation, the tier and the
 time. No text is kept, so none is shown.
- Qualité (`/memory/quality`), org and teams only: stale entries (not
 updated in the threshold), contested facts (one title, two different
 texts in one tier), duplicates (one title in several tiers, or one text
 twice), orphan tags (a tag of a controlled namespace that names none of
 its values). An entry opens in Notes and can be archived
 (`POST /api/v1/memory/admin/entries/archive`, audited `archive`; a
 person's tier is refused). Below the lists, the measures of lot A.8
 (section "Quality page, the measures").
- Journal (`/memory/journal`): the memory audit, filtered by person,
 action, tier (`org`, `team:*`, `user:*`), outcome and dates, paged with a
 ` | ` cursor, exported as CSV with the same filters
 (`/api/v1/memory/admin/journal/export`, audited `journal_export`).
- Ma mémoire and Parcourir became Notes (2026-10-11, section "Console:
 Notes"); their addresses redirect there.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Console: Notes (2026-10-11, writable everywhere since 2026-10-12)
sections.text:
Mémoire > Notes (`/console/memory/notes`, every signed-in person) reads the
memory with exactly the access of the tools: one's own tier, org and one's
teams (an admin every team), never another person's tier, an admin's
included. Every note one reads is written in place.
- The sidebar: a search over title, text, folder and tags (accents
 ignored), the notes pinned and opened recently in this browser, then each
 tier with its folders (topics) and notes, one line each; a + beside a
 tier or a folder starts a new note there.
- The note is a live preview editor (CodeMirror 6, its own chunk): the
 markdown is drawn as it reads and shown as source on the lines the cursor
 is on. `[[` lists the notes one reads (title, tier, folder); Enter writes
 `[[Title]]`. Cmd or Ctrl+click follows a link (`[[Title]]`,
 `[[topic/name]]`, `[[id]]`, an alias after `|`, a markdown link to a
 note's file or console address); a link to nothing one reads is muted.
 Enter continues a list, a checkbox toggles, Cmd or Ctrl+S saves now, undo
 and redo are the editor's. The title is the heading above (Enter or
 leaving it renames); the tags are chips with a × and a + that offers the
 vocabularies (`GET /api/v1/memory/read/tags`) and the tags in use; one's
 own folder is a chip that moves the note (its id stays). Mentions end the
 note: each note citing it, with the line that cites it. An outline rail
 of the headings shows from 1280 px.
- Saving: 800 ms after the typing stops, on leaving the editor and on
 leaving the note; the bar says Enregistrement…, Enregistré, Hors ligne,
 en attente (tried again every 4 s and when the browser is back online),
 Modifiée ailleurs, or Non enregistrée with the reason in words (a secret,
 personal information the organization blocks, an unknown tag). A value
 the filter masks comes back masked and the page says so. Each save names
 the version it was made on; a note changed elsewhere answers 409
 `memory_conflict` and the page offers Recharger (take the other version)
 or Garder la mienne (write over it).
- Shared notes: an edit of an org or team note applies at once when the
 caller is a person and the auto-accept rules let them (a member into
 their team, an admin into org, Politiques), else it becomes one review
 item that later edits replace; a console session viewing as someone else
 always sends the shared note for review. The page says "Envoyée pour
 revue" with a link to the proposal and shows that waiting edit as the
 person's draft when they come back. A shared note keeps its folder (an
 admin moves it). Archive: one's own note, and an org or team note for an
 admin. An encrypted note (the private E2E tier) is read only here: it is
 edited where its key lives.
- Carte (`?view=map`): the links on a canvas, coloured by tier, a find
 field, a legend that hides a tier; a click opens a note.
- Cmd or Ctrl+O: the quick switcher. Cmd or Ctrl+N (or Alt with it): a new
 note, in place (tier, folder, title, text; Create, or Send for review

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Contested facts (A.8)
sections.text:
A write, rewrite or approval that makes an entry active with the same title
(case, accents and spaces folded) as another active entry and a different
body flags both (`memory_contested`). Compared: the same tier and `org` (an
`org` entry: `org` and the teams), never another person's own tier. A recall
hit carries `contested: true`. The nightly rollup closes a pair once one
side is archived, the titles differ or the bodies agree.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Directory (A.2)
sections.text:
Nightly (and `POST /api/v1/memory/admin/directory/rebuild`), the server
writes `org/directory/ .md` for every listed team with entries: its
topics and tags with their counts and the `directory_title` its entries
publish, each with a path. Never a body. A team marked unlisted
(`PUT /api/v1/memory/admin/teams/{id}`) has no file. A file is rewritten only
when its text changes. Recall finds them ("which team holds
client:<name>").

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Duplicate detector (A.8)
sections.text:
When a `memory_recall`, a `work_check` or a Sagax prompt
(`POST /api/v1/memory/duplicates`) arrives, its intent is compared with the
work log of the last 30 days: the words of the text (lowercase, accents
folded, French and English stop words dropped, a plural `s` dropped), its
tags and its object ids. Candidates come from the full text index of the
intents (`memory_work_fts`, FTS5, migration 0057) and from the object refs;
no model and no vector store (DEC-3; no embeddings exist on an install
today, FTS5 is the guaranteed mode of analysis 17.12). The score, 0 to 1:
the same object is the same work (0.7, plus 0.3 times the best of the
words and tags in common); otherwise three quarters words (the mean of Dice
and of the overlap over the shorter intent, nothing under two shared words)
and a quarter tags (Jaccard), over the features the query has. A hint needs
`memory_dup_threshold` (50 %); at most three, best first; the person's own
event of the last hour is the same session and is left out.
A hint: `hint_id`, `pointer` (`work: `), `day`, `who` (`you`,
`participant` for a thread participant, `team `, or `a colleague`),
`score`, `matched_on` (`text`, `tags`, `objects`) and `readable`. Only for a
tier the person reads: `intent`, `tool`, `action`, `result`, `objects`,
`link`. An event of a tier the person does not read (another person's own
tier, a team they are not in) gives the bare pointer and nothing else; the
way to the work is `ask_person` with `person: "work: "`, which reaches its
author while the asker sees the pointer, never the name (`via_pointer` on the
question). A thread with several participants reads what every one of them
reads (analysis 17.6). `memory_dup_hints` = `readable` keeps only the tiers
the person reads, `off` turns the detector off.
The fate of each hint is stored (`memory_dup_hints`): `accepted` when the
person opens the pointer (`work_open`, `ask_person` through it) or answers
`same` (the work avoided), `dismissed` (`different`, `dismiss`), `ignored` when
nobody answered within a day. A linked Sagax server sends the verdicts and
the cards a turn used with `POST /api/v1/memory/feedback`:
 
and checks a prompt before the turn with `POST /api/v1/memory/duplicates`
(`person`, `text` at most 4 000 characters, never stored, `tags`, `objects`,
`participants`), which answers `turn`, `duplicates` and `next`. Both take the
link token.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Entry format
sections.text:
A file with another `schema` is refused, not guessed. A file edited by hand
is picked up by the next reindex. A `tiers` entry repeats a third party and
is never served as a procedure.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Export and erasure (A.2)
sections.text:
- A person exports their own tier (`GET /api/v1/memory/me/export`); an admin
 exports a person's from the person sheet (audited). A `tar.gz` of markdown:
 `memory/` and `archive/`. An encrypted private tier (lot A.9) leaves as
 stored: sealed bodies and an `ENCRYPTION.json` manifest, never decrypted.
- Erasure (person sheet, `POST /api/v1/memory/admin/people/{id}/erase` with
 the login typed again): the tier and its archive, the person's pending
 items, their questions, their audience and channel. Their contributions to
 shared tiers stay with their provenance by default (decision 11);
 `team_contributions: "remove"` deletes them. Tombstones
 (`memory_tombstones`) are replayed by every reindex, so a restored backup
 never brings erased content back: after a restore, always run
 `memory reindex`. The git history of org and teams keeps a removed shared
 entry until the history is rewritten (an operator task).

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Guardrails (A.9)
sections.text:
### End-to-end encryption of the private tier
With `memory_private_e2e` at `optional` or `required`, the body of an entry
of a person's own tier is stored sealed under a key Perspicax never keeps.
The promise: nobody reads it without the person's key, the console admin and
the VM operator included, a disk snapshot included. What stays in clear by
design: the header (topic, tags, a generic title `Entrée chiffrée` unless
the client sets one) and the `searchable` text the client chooses to send,
which is all the index holds. Put nothing private in them.
- The key: 32 bytes derived on the client from a passphrase
 (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 600 000 rounds, salt = the first 16 bytes of
 `SHA-256("pxm-e2e/1 salt" || 0x00 || user id)`) or a device key (32
 random bytes in the Keychain or DPAPI). The client presents it with every
 request in the `X-Perspicax-Memory-Key` header (base64). Caddy drops that
 header from its access log (`deploy/Caddyfile`, `infra/runtime/Caddyfile`);
 any other edge must do the same.
- Enrollment: the first sealed write records the key id (16 hex of
 `SHA-256("pxm-e2e/1 key-id" || 0x00 || key)`) in the setting
 `memory_e2e_key: `. From then on, a write without the key, or with
 another key, is refused (`memory_locked`, `memory_key_wrong`); `required`
 refuses a write without a key even before enrollment.
- Sealing: XChaCha20-Poly1305, a fresh 24-byte nonce, AAD
 `pxm-e2e/1\n \n \n `. The client may seal itself
 and send the armor as the body (`memory_write` then receives no text at
 all), or send the text with the key and `searchable` (the server seals in
 memory; the secret gate and the PII policy read the text first). The
 armor, the body of the entry file:
- Reading: `memory_recall`, `memory_search`, `related_memory` and the
 Claude memory tool search the tier only when the session presents the
 enrolled key; otherwise they answer without it and name it in `locked`.
 A thread with several people never carries the key. A promotion to a team
 opens the entry with the key (the person chooses to share it); a sealed
 body is never sent to a shared tier (`memory_sealed_shared`).
- Export and erasure: the export holds the sealed files and
 `ENCRYPTION.json` (format, key id, KDF parameters). Erasure deletes the
 files and the key id: what a snapshot kept is unreadable without the key.
- Not covered: the work log (`work/`, structured events) stays in clear;
 forgetting the passphrase loses the tier (no recovery by design); the
 consolidation of a private tier (A.6) must run on the person's client.
### Keys outside the disk (Azure Key Vault)
- Vault master key: `vault_key_provider = keyvault` and
 `PXC_VAULT_KEY_URI=https:// .vault.azure.net/secrets/ `. The
 key (`v : `, the format of `state/vault.key`) is read at
 boot and kept in memory only. Memory salt: `memory_salt_uri` (or
 `PXC_MEMORY_SALT_URI`), at least 16 characters; when an install already
 has a local salt, copy its value (`memory_actor_salt`) into the secret

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Inbox and review (A.2)
sections.text:
A write to `org` or a team lands in that tier's inbox with a `source`:
`tiers` when any `derived_from` item is a `ticket_note`, an `email` or a
`vendor_text`; else `humain` when `written_by_person`; else `interne`
(`tool`, `bot`, `routine`, `work_log`, `memory`, `person`). It is accepted at
once when it is not `tiers`, the writer is a person (not a Sagax agent, not
an automated OAuth client, and not a console session viewing as someone
else) and the writer may: a member
(or an admin) into a team, an admin into org. A bot's write stays in the
inbox, even when `written_by_person` is set. Everything else waits, with
`memory_propose` items and promotions, in one queue:
- a write that lands in the inbox (`state: "inbox"`) and every proposal
 (`status: "proposed"`) answer a `next` naming `memory_review` with the
 review id: the author follows it with `action show` (or `list` with
 `mine`), a reviewer answers it; an accepted or unscanned write has no
 `next`;
- a manager reviews the teams they manage, an admin org and every team;
- approve, approve with an edit (title, body, tags: gated again), merge into
 an existing entry (`merged_from`), refuse with a reason (the waiting file
 is deleted), return to the author (the item lands in their own tier);
- at most `memory_review_cap_week` (50) items waiting per author per week
 (`memory_review_cap_reached`); a pending item expires after
 `memory_review_expiry_days` (14) and returns to its author (nightly);
- a risk score at entry: `tiers` +3, a directory person's name +2, a
 credential-like token the gate let through +3; from 2 on an item is
 risky and never part of a bulk approval;
- a promotion moves the entry: approved, the origin is archived and the new
 entry keeps `promoted_from` and its provenance; only a person promotes
 (`memory_bot` otherwise);
- the tag `personal` never enters a shared tier (`memory_personal`).
An A.1 proposal without a review row joins the queue at the next listing.
### Bot exception for shared topics
Off by default: with `memory_bot_shared_topics` empty (and
`PXC_MEMORY_BOT_SHARED_TOPICS` unset) nothing changes. When it is set (a
comma list, e.g. `gox`; the settings row, set by an admin through
`PATCH /api/v1/settings` and audited, wins over the environment), a NEW
entry an agent (a Sagax agent or another automated client acting for a
person) writes to a shared tier is published at once instead of
waiting, when all hold:
- the entry topic is in the list and an entry tag is that topic (`gox`,
 `topic:gox` or `category:gox`, case-insensitive);
- the scope kind is in `memory_bot_shared_scopes` (`team`, `org`; env
 `PXC_MEMORY_BOT_SHARED_SCOPES`). Unset means `team` only: org is reached
 only when `org` is named;
- for a team, the person the agent acts for is a member of it (admin rights
 do not count);
- the call is an agent (`Access::human` false, not impersonating): a person goes through the normal rule,
 a console session viewing as someone never qualifies;

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Injection budget (A.2)
sections.text:
`memory_recall` and `related_memory` fit `memory_injection_budget_tokens`
(1 500, estimated at 4 bytes a token): directory pointers first, then
entries by rank, cut from the end; a cut recall says `truncated: true`.
`related_memory` keeps its own 400 characters at most.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Later lots
sections.text:
`memory.*` permission keys in the catalogue (after the Sagax permission sets
land), the Sagax context card and the persona editor's Memory category
(Sagax side); the consolidations page with its diffs
(A.6, the schedule is already a policy); consolidation (A.6); import (A.7).
Lots A.3, A.4, A.8 and A.9 are above; still open after them: the Sagax side
of the key (derivation, Keychain or DPAPI, the header), the bootstrap switch
to the `keyvault` provider on GOX, the Sagax side of A.8 (calling the prompt
check before a turn and sending the feedback, Sagax's own lot), federation
(study only).

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Layout
sections.text:
The topics `inbox` and `directory` are the server's: nobody writes to them.
The inboxes stay out of git (`/org/inbox/`, `/teams/*/inbox/` in the
`.gitignore`, added to an A.1 file at the next start): a refused write must
not linger in the history.
The folder is created at the first start (mode 0700). The git repository is
local to the server, has no remote and is never pushed. Without the `git`
binary (the image ships it) the memory works unversioned and the backup has
no bundle.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Measures (A.8)
sections.text:
A memory turn is a recall, a `related_memory` block, a `work_check` or a
Sagax prompt check. Each records (`memory_turns`, `memory_turn_cards`): the
tokens it added to the client's context (the serialized answer, 4 bytes a
token), the client family, the cards it offered (`entry: / `,
`work: `, `hint: `) and later the cards used: opened (`work_open`) or
cited (`memory_feedback`, the Sagax feedback) within seven days. A salted
actor hash ties a card to its person; no body, query or prompt is stored.
Raw turns are kept 90 days, hints 365.
The nightly pass (after the governance pass) and the Quality page's
Recompute write daily rollups (`memory_measure_daily`, UTC days, counts
only): turns, tokens, cards offered and used (work cards apart), hints
offered, accepted, dismissed, ignored, new contested facts, and the A.0
measure replayed on the journal (`gateway::memory::dupes`): MCP calls,
targeted object events, cross-person duplicate episodes counted on the day
of their first event in the ISO week (so a week's days add up to the A.0
weekly figure), their bytes, and writes after another person's write. The
replay follows annex B of
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-duplicate-work-measure.md` except that the
bytes of an `api_result_query` are not given back to the handle's request.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Obsidian and git sync (A.4)
sections.text:
Every tier a person reads is served to them as a git repository over HTTPS
(the smart HTTP protocol), so they can keep a copy on their computer, open
it in Obsidian, change a line and push it back:
 
The password (HTTP Basic, any user name, or a `Bearer`) is a token of the
person: a memory sync token (console Mémoire > Synchro Obsidian,
`/console/memory/sync`, or `POST /api/v1/memory/sync/token`; 90 days, shown
once, a new one revokes the previous), another API token of theirs, or a
console session. A memory sync token (`sessions.scope = memory_sync`) opens
the git routes and `/api/v1/memory/sync/*` only: never `/mcp`, never the
rest of the API, and it cannot mint another one. A tier the person does not
read answers 404; a push where they do not write answers 403. A linked
Sagax server's token, a service account and a system account get nothing.
A linked Sagax mints that token for the person signed in to it, so nobody
pastes it by hand: `POST /api/v1/pulsabot/people/{sub}/memory-sync-token`
with its link token (`Authorization: Bearer`, the link file's
`link_token`; a console cookie is never read) mints or rotates the memory
sync token of the directory person `sub` exactly as their own route does
(client `memory-sync`, scope `memory_sync`, 90 days, the live one revoked),
answers `{token, info}` once with `Cache-Control: no-store`, and writes one
`admin_audit` row `pulsabot.memory_sync_token.mint` (target the server,
`after {sub, session_id}`, never the token) and the person's
`memory_sync_token_minted` auth event (client `pulsa-bot: `).
An unknown `sub`, a service account, a link account and a person marked
system answer `404 {"error":"no_person"}`; a disabled person `409
{"error":"user_inactive"}`.
What a clone holds: the tier's active entries (` / .md`, the files
as the server keeps them), its generated `MEMORY.md`, a generated
`.gitignore` (`.obsidian/`, `.trash/`, `.DS_Store`, `*.tmp`) and, in a
shared tier, the person's own items waiting for a review under
`_pending/ .md`. Never another person's pending item, never an inbox,
never a private tier but one's own.
A private tier sealed end to end (lot A.9) clones as its sealed armor and is
read only over git: a push to it is refused, the person writes it from a
client that holds their key.
What a push does (the receive hook, `gateway::memory::sync`):
- The pack is indexed into a quarantine directory; nothing reaches the
 mirror before the push is accepted, so a refused secret never stays on
 the server.
- One branch, `main`, fast-forward only. A push from a clone that did not
 pull the server's last commit is refused with `fetch first`.
- Every changed path must be ` / .md` (topic: lowercase letters,
 digits and hyphens; not `inbox` nor `directory`). `MEMORY.md`,
 `.gitignore`, `_pending/` and `org/directory/` are generated, read only.
 Anything else (another extension, a deeper folder, a hidden file, a link,
 a submodule) refuses the push with `memory_path_refused`.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation)
sections.text:
Operator guide of the memory shipped by lots A.1 (foundation), A.2
(tiers and governance), A.3 (secret and PII filter), A.4 (Obsidian and
the local cache) and A.8 (duplicate detector and measures, against the
baseline of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-duplicate-work-measure.md`) of
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-09-master-implementation-plan.md` (detailed
plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-09-memory-foundation-plan.md` and
`2026-10-09-memory-tiers-plan.md`; design:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-perspicax-memory-analysis.md`).
The memory is a set of markdown files on the Perspicax server. Every MCP
client (claude.ai, Claude Code, Cursor, Sagax, any other) reads and writes it
through built-in tools, under the identity of the person signed in. The
database only indexes, authorizes and journals; it is rebuilt from the files
at any time.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Quality page, the measures (A.8)
sections.text:
The measures are a section of Mémoire > Qualité (admins), below the lists of
lot A.5 (section "Console (A.5)", `GET /api/v1/memory/admin/quality`):
`GET /api/v1/memory/admin/quality/measures`, Recompute
`POST /api/v1/memory/admin/quality/measures/refresh` (35 days), detector
settings `PUT /api/v1/memory/admin/quality/settings` (`threshold_pct` 30 to
95, `reach` all, readable, off; audited like every setting).
- The pursue criterion of the measure doc (section 7), over the last 28
 days: pursue when the cross-person duplicates reach 150 a week and 5 %
 of the pointers shown are followed (hints accepted plus work cards used,
 over hints offered plus work cards offered), or when the duplicate
 rate (episodes per targeted event) is at least 20 % under the A.0 rate
 (1 162 / 11 400 = 10.2 %); else stop. Provisional before 30 days of
 measures.
- Decision 13: stop when fewer than 5 % of the cards offered are used after
 60 days (provisional before).
- Tiles over 30 days: tokens per turn, cards used, hints, work avoided,
 contested facts, cross-person duplicates.
- The weekly duplicates next to the A.0 weeks (W39 188, W40 514, W41 460 in
 4.6 days; writes 8, 21, 95; targeted events 2 085, 4 534, 4 781).
- The avoided work of 30 days: day, how, surface, tier kind and score.
Each verdict shows its reasons with the numbers. Purpose (analysis 17.11):
whether the memory is worth it, never a measure of a person; no view per
person exists.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Reindex and integrity
sections.text:
On the GOX VM: `docker compose exec -T connector pulsatrix-connector memory
reindex`. The console's Mémoire overview has the same rebuild button. A
reindex is idempotent; a file with a broken header, a header that disagrees
with its place, or a second file for the same key is skipped and listed.
The nightly loop (03:00 local, after retention and backup) runs the check and
keeps the result in `memory_last_integrity_at` and
`memory_last_integrity_result`, shown on the overview.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Secret and PII filter (A.3)
sections.text:
Every memory write (`memory_write`, `memory_propose`, the `memory` tool's
file commands), review edit, review reason, `ask_person` question and
answer, and Sagax work intent runs the filter (`gateway::memory::filter`,
`Memory::screen`; an import (lot A.7) calls the same function). Layers, the
first that hits refuses:
1. Vault: the connector's redactor when the caller has one, then the vault
 fingerprints. Every value of `credentials`, `email_secrets`,
 `pulsabot_provider_keys` and `products.mcp_headers` (JSON slots split,
 naming slots such as `username`, `client_id`, `url` left out) is kept as
 HMAC-SHA256 under a per-install salt, 128 bits: one `value` print for a
 value of 6 to 15 bytes, a `gram` print every 4 bytes for each 12-byte
 window of a value of 12 bytes or more (a copy of 15 bytes or more is found
 anywhere in a text). A save through the model fingerprints the new value
 at once; a rebuild (at start, and whenever the sealed rows change) marks
 the prints of a value no longer present `retired`, which still blocks
 (`vault_value_retired`). The salt is sealed by the vault
 (`memory_filter_salts`); `gateway rotate-vault` re-seals it and adds the
 next version, kept with the older ones for their retired prints. Values
 under 6 bytes are not fingerprinted. Never the value, never which
 credential.
2. Rules (`filter/rules.rs`, always block): the main gitleaks rule set
 ported to Rust (AWS, Azure client secrets, SAS and storage keys, GitHub,
 GitLab, Slack, Stripe, private keys, JWT, bearer and basic headers,
 connection strings, credentials in URLs, about 50 vendor shapes, the
 generic keyed assignment with Shannon entropy 3.5) and the bilingual
 keyword rules: a password word (mot de passe, mdp, password, PSK, clé
 WPA, Wi-Fi, ...) followed by a value that reads as a password, a PIN word
 (NIP, PIN, code d'alarme, ...) followed by 4 to 8 digits, a key word
 (secret, jeton, clé API, ...) followed by a long value, a TOTP seed, a
 BitLocker recovery key. "Le mot de passe est dans le coffre" passes.
3. Personal information: built-in detectors (credit cards with Luhn, NAS
 with Luhn or after its keyword, NAM/RAMQ with its date, IBAN with its
 check, email, phone, date of birth after its keyword, and keyword forms
 for SSN, bank account, passport and driver's license), then the Presidio
 sidecar when `memory_pii_mode` is not `off` (section "PII sidecar").
 Each finding falls in a category of Politiques (`government_id`,
 `health`, `financial`, `date_of_birth`, `email`, `phone`, `person_name`,
 `postal_address`) whose action applies: `allow`, `mask`
 (`[redacted: ]` replaces the span before the write; a sidecar
 finding without a range refuses instead), `quarantine` or `refuse` (both
 refuse the write and keep only its hash). The default action is
 `quarantine`. Contacts (email, phone, person name, postal address) pass
 unless the mode is `strict` and the entry has no `person:` tag. A

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Settings
sections.text:
Console: Mémoire, or `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/memory/admin/settings` (admins,
audited like every setting).
| Setting | Default | Effect |
 
| `memory_enabled` | on | `off` hides the tools from every caller and stops the work log |
| `memory_related` | on | `off` drops `related_memory` |
| `memory_cap_org_entries`, `memory_cap_org_bytes` | 2 000, 20 MB | past either cap a write is refused with `memory_cap_reached` |
| `memory_cap_team_entries`, `memory_cap_team_bytes` | 5 000, 50 MB | per team |
| `memory_cap_user_entries`, `memory_cap_user_bytes` | 5 000, 50 MB | per person |
Proposals and inbox items count against their target tier; archived
entries do not.
Governance (lot A.2): `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/memory/admin/governance`
(`review_cap_week` 50, `review_expiry_days` 14, `injection_budget_tokens`
1 500), audited like every setting.
Guardrails (lot A.9), all off by default, in the console Settings or
`PATCH /api/v1/settings` (admins, audited):
| Setting | Default | Effect |
 
| `memory_private_e2e` | `off` | `optional` or `required`: end-to-end encryption of the private tier (below) |
| `memory_pii_mode` | `off` | `sensitive` or `strict`: the mode of the PII sidecar (below; named `memory_pii_policy` before lot A.3, which holds the per-category actions of Politiques) |
| `memory_pii_presidio_url` | empty | the analyzer base URL; empty reads `PXC_PRESIDIO_URL` |
| `memory_salt_uri` | empty | the Key Vault secret of the memory salt; empty reads `PXC_MEMORY_SALT_URI`, then the local salt |
Detector (lot A.8): `memory_dup_threshold` (50, percent, 30 to 95) and
`memory_dup_hints` (`all`, `readable`, `off`), through
`PUT /api/v1/memory/admin/quality/settings`.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Tags (A.2)
sections.text:
Namespaces are the organization's (console Mémoire > Tags, or
`/api/v1/memory/admin/tags`): a label in each language, a source (`manual`,
or `connector: : `), controlled or free, required on shared
writes or not. A tag `ns:value` of a controlled namespace must name a value
or a synonym (rewritten to its value); an unknown one is refused with the
closest values (`memory_tag_unknown`). A tag of an undefined namespace and a
bare tag pass. Filters accept `ns:*`. `personal` and `procedure` are never
namespaces. Tags classify, they never authorize.
A connector namespace is synced read only through the connector's own
dispatch, as its `source_config.run_as` person (their profiles and
credentials), paged 100 at a time, each value slugged, nightly and from the
console's Synchroniser button. For GOX, `client` from the ConnectWise
companies:
 
(the `tool` and `resource` are the ones `api_search` shows on the install).
Synced values no longer served are removed when every page was read;
manual values are never touched.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Tools
sections.text:
Listed to directory persons in every service mode while the memory is on.
| Tool | Purpose |
 
| `memory_recall` | Ranked full text over the tiers one reads; `include_work` adds matching work log events |
| `memory_search` | Tags, topic, creation window |
| `work_search` | Work log events by object (`cw_psa_service:tickets:12345` or a bare id), actor kind, window |
| `memory_write` | A short fact: `scope` `me`, `org` or `team: ` (omitted: the audience of section "Audiences"); `derived_from`, `directory_title` |
| `memory_propose` | A fact proposed to org or a team (always reviewed) |
| `memory_promote` | Move an entry up: own tier to a team one belongs to, a team to org (reviewed). A bot is refused (`memory_bot`) |
| `memory_review` | The review queue: `list`, `show`, `approve` (edit, `merge_into`), `refuse`, `return`, `bulk_approve` |
| `memory_forget` | Archive one of one's own entries |
| `memory` | The Claude API memory tool commands (`view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `delete`, `rename`) over `/memories/org` and `/memories/team/ ` (read only) and `/memories/me` (read and write) |
| `ask_person` | Ask a colleague (section "ask_person"); with `question_id`, where it stands; `person: "work: "` reaches the author of a duplicate hint without naming them (A.8) |
| `work_check` | Before a task: is someone on it, or was someone on it in the last 30 days (section "Duplicate detector") |
| `work_open` | Open a work pointer `work: `: the event when one reads its tier, else its day and the `ask_person` route |
| `memory_feedback` | The cards of a turn one relied on or cited (`used`), or the verdict on a hint (`same`, `different`, `dismiss`) |
Recall hits carry `served_as`: `procedure` (topic `procedure...`, tag
`procedure`, `skill:` or `guide:`), `fact`, or `third_party` for a `tiers`
entry, which a client never follows as a procedure. Since A.8 a hit may carry
`contested: true` (section "Contested facts"), and a recall answers
`duplicates` (at most three hints), `next` and `turn`.
Every write passes the secret and PII filter (section "Secret and PII
filter"). A refusal names a rule; the quarantine and the audit keep the rule
and a sha256, never the text.
The journal row of a memory call keeps the topic, scope and tags, never a
body, a query or an excerpt.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Upgrade guard (0049)
sections.text:
Migration 0049 is forward only: a binary older than this version refuses a
store at schema 49 (`newer than this binary`). Snapshot the data disk and run
`gateway backup` before deploying, as for 0048.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Upgrade guard (0052)
sections.text:
Migration 0052 (lot A.2) rebuilds the `memory_entries` index (state
`inbox`) and adds the governance tables. Numbered 52: 51 belongs to the Sagax
permission sets of another lane and must be applied first (the runner skips
a version at or below the store's), so a release carries both or 51 first.
Forward only: a binary older than 52 refuses the store. Snapshot the data
disk and run `gateway backup` before deploying.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Upgrade guard (0053)
sections.text:
Migration 0053 (lot A.3) adds `memory_filter_salts` and
`memory_filter_queue` (both sealed by the vault and re-sealed by
`gateway rotate-vault`), `memory_secret_prints` and `memory_quarantine`.
Forward only: a binary older than 53 refuses the store. Snapshot the data
disk and run `gateway backup` before deploying; 0051 and 0052 must reach
the store first. The first start fingerprints the vault (one rebuild, logged
`memory filter: vault fingerprints rebuilt`).

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Upgrade guard (0057)
sections.text:
Migration 0057 (lot A.8) adds `tags` to `memory_work_events`, the intent
index `memory_work_fts` (filled from the existing rows), `memory_dup_hints`,
`memory_turns`, `memory_turn_cards`, `memory_contested`,
`memory_measure_daily` and `memory_questions.via_pointer`. The list reads
52, 53, 56, 57 (54 and 55 are unused: lots A.4 and A.5 held them and shipped
without a migration); 53 and 56 reach a store before 57 (the runner skips a
version at or below the store's), which one release carrying all of them
guarantees. Forward only; snapshot the data disk and run `gateway backup`
before deploying.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Who reads and writes what
sections.text:
Resolved at every call from the signed-in identity (never from a client
argument):
| Person | Reads | Writes | Reviews |
 
| Employee | org, the teams they belong to, their own tier | their own tier; org and their teams through the inbox | nothing |
| Manager | the same | the same | the items of the teams they manage |
| Admin | org, every team, their own tier | their own tier; org and any team through the inbox | org and every team |
Nobody reads another person's tier, an admin neither, the console included
(the export of section "Export and erasure" is a file, audited). Service
accounts, linked Sagax servers and system accounts get no memory tool.
A Sagax agent (MCP client `pulsa-bot: `), an automated OAuth
client (`ai-thread:*`, and any OAuth client other than the console) and
a console session viewing as someone else write under that person's
identity, but a write to org or a team is never published directly: it
stays in the inbox until a person promotes it (`memory_promote`, or the
console Propositions). A bot that promotes or approves is refused
(`memory_bot`). A personal `pxat1.` API token cannot be told from a
person in this version: it is treated as human.
In a thread with several participants (a Sagax room), a client passes
`participants` (user ids) to `memory_recall` or `memory_search`: the read is
then org plus the teams every participant reads, and never a private tier
(analysis 17.6). A participant who is not a directory person reads org
only.

sections.title: Perspicax: Organization memory (foundation): Work log
sections.text:
Every vendor write that goes through the connector (create, update, delete,
action) adds one event in the actor's home tier (their first team by id, else
their own tier): a salted actor hash, person or bot, the product, the
operation id, the action, the object ids of the path, the request body and the
created object, the result and the HTTP status. Never free text.
A linked Sagax server adds bot runs and routine runs with
`POST /api/v1/memory/work` under its link token:
 
At most 50 rows; `action` one of create, update, delete, action, run, turn,
other; `result` one of ok, error, refused, partial; the intent one line of
at most 140 characters, checked by the secret gate. The batch is refused as a
whole on the first bad row.
`api_search` and `api_plan` answers carry `related_memory`: at most five
pointers ("done by team X on (work: )", "procedure: ") and 400
characters, from the work log on the ids of the plan and from the procedures
(topic `procedure...`, tag `procedure`, `skill:` or `guide:`) a full text
search of the query finds.

sections.title: Perspicax: Sagax (Perspicax as identity provider): Accounts the directory sees
sections.text:
`account_kind` is derived, not a column:
| Kind | Who |
 
| `person` | `kind = person` and not marked system |
| `service_account` | a `service` account that is not a linked server, or a person an admin marked system (`PUT /api/v1/users/{id}/system`) |
| `linked_server` | the service user of a `pulsabot_servers` row |
The Sagax directory is persons only. A marked system account leaves every
people picker, the directory and Members. The link account never reaches
`/mcp` (401) and is 403 on every other `/api/v1` route.
Avatars: Perspicax stores a version (first 16 hex of the image SHA-256).
Sagax reads `GET /api/v1/pulsabot/people/{sub}/avatar` with the link
token. The `pulsa-bot` `id_token` carries `picture` under `profile` when
the person has one.

sections.title: Perspicax: Sagax (Perspicax as identity provider): Bot rights
sections.text:
`users.sagax_bots` is `manage` (default, every existing and new account) or
`use`. Perspicax stores and serves it; Sagax enforces it.
- `manage`: create, import, duplicate, edit, delete and own bots.
- `use`: read-only. Only bots shared with the person, paid by their own
 model credentials.
`PUT /api/v1/users/{id}/sagax-bots { sagax_bots }` (admin). Audited
`user.sagax_bots.allow` or `user.sagax_bots.restrict`, refusals too.
Refused on oneself, on a `service` account and on a person marked as a
system account (400), on a link account (409). The directory and
`GET /api/v1/pulsabot/members` carry the value (the directory `ETag`
follows it).

sections.title: Perspicax: Sagax (Perspicax as identity provider): Console map
sections.text:
Read from the console navigation (`console/src/components/shell.tsx`, the
`NAV` constant, 2026-10-10: eight entries, the account menu and the settings
window) and its routes (`console/src/main.tsx`). A row flagged Sagax shows
only while a server is linked (`GET /api/v1/pulsabot/linked` lists one); an
admin sees it anyway, and the page says how to link a server. Entry and tab
names are the French ones of `console/src/lib/messages.fr.ts`.
| Feature | Where (entry, then page) | Who |
 
| Linked servers: link, renew the link token (bundle shown once), unlink | Paramètres, Organisation, Configuration des bots (`/sagax/settings`, tab Serveurs; a server's sheet `?server= &stab=`, tabs Aperçu and Lien) | admin, even with no server linked |
